backward_compat_traps.Gen1_device: Trains at 2.5 GT/s only; Polling.Speed sub-state stays at 2.5 GT/s.
backward_compat_traps.Gen2plus_device: Trains at 2.5 GT/s first; then negotiates Recovery.Speed up to its maximum.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Gen 2+ device on a Gen 1 Link will silently fall back to 2.5 GT/s — bandwidth surprise for users.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Both ends advertise their max lane width via TS1/TS2; agreement is the minimum.
backward_compat_traps.trap: x16 device on a x4 Link silently trains as x4 — performance surprise.
Gen 3+ silicon must implement BOTH encoders to remain backward-compatible; a Gen 3 PHY only running 128b/130b will not train against a Gen 1 partner.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Max_Payload_Size_Supported is advertised; runtime Max_Payload_Size is set to the minimum across the path from Requester to Completer.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Endpoint advertises 4096 B, but a Switch in the path only supports 128 B → the path must run at 128 B; misconfiguration causes Malformed TLP errors.

backward_compat_traps.rule: ASPM, ECRC, Vendor-Specific Messages, Hot-Plug, MSI vs MSI-X — each must be discovered via Capability Structures and explicitly enabled.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Assuming a peer supports ASPM L1 without checking Link Capabilities will cause traffic to stall or hang.

previous_versions: PCI Local Bus Specification 2.3 (predecessor parallel-bus standard; PCIe inherits its software model)

key_changes.summary: First production PCI Express base specification. Introduces serial differential 2.5 GT/s point-to-point Links, 8b/10b encoding, layered Transaction/DataLink/Physical architecture, TLP + DLLP packetization, credit-based flow control, Virtual Channels (1-8) + Traffic Classes (8), Switch + Endpoint + Root Complex device classes, LTSSM, ASPM (L0s + L1) + software-controlled link PM (L2/L3), native hot-plug, Advanced Error Reporting (AER), and PCI-compatible Configuration Space + 4 KB Extended Configuration Space.

future_versions_industry_outline.summary: Doubles per-Lane raw bandwidth to 5 GT/s; same 8b/10b encoding (20% overhead); backward-compatible with 1.0/1.1 devices via auto-negotiation.
Switches encoding to 128b/130b (much lower 1.5% overhead); raw 8 GT/s gives ~7.88 Gb/s effective per Lane.
Doubles to 16 GT/s; same 128b/130b encoding; tighter channel-loss budget.
Doubles to 32 GT/s; NRZ; introduces precoding option for SerDes.
Switches NRZ to PAM4 (4 levels per UI); adds Forward Error Correction (FEC); FLIT-based packet flow.
Doubles to 128 GT/s; new channel-loss budget; FLIT-based mandatory.

fields.version_naming_history_note: NVMe is managed by NVM Express, Inc., a 501(c)(6) industry association founded in 2009 (announced 2011). NVMe-oF and NVMe-MI are sister specifications. NVMe 2.0 (May 2021, after this Base 1.4 doc) restructured into Base + per-Command-Set specs + per-Transport bindings.

spec_lineage_nvme_base.summary: Initial NVMe Base; PCIe register-level interface; SQ/CQ; 64-byte command + 16-byte completion; PRP; Admin + NVM.
Added SGL, Autonomous Power State Transition, Multi-Path I/O / Namespace Sharing.
Added Namespace Management & Attachment, CMB, HMB, Live Firmware Activation, Telemetry, Streams.
Added Boot Partitions, Sanitize, Directives, Virtualization Enhancements (SR-IOV), Self-Test, Telemetry HI/CI.
Added PMR, ANA, Endurance Groups, NVM Sets, Predictable Latency, Get LBA Status, IO Determinism, Read Recovery Level.

spec_lineage_nvme_over_fabrics.summary: Defines NVMe over Fabrics; RDMA + Fibre Channel; Capsule format, Connect, Property Get/Set, Discovery service.

spec_lineage_nvme_mi.summary: Management Interface; SMBus / PCIe VDM / MCTP transports.
